sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Mollyndroat is a Manx folkloric figure. In the tale of the Isle of Man a giant served an evil druid, and that giant is Mollyndroat. The story is close to the European tale of Rumpelstiltskin. The giant held a woman captive and would not set her free until she guessed his name. The figure may be tied to the evil giant Meleagant, also known as Mellyagraunce, who carried off queen Guinevere in the Arthurian legend.
